title-proc.eng: Pre-commercial Procurement of an innovative Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations (suHCO)

description-proc.eng: suHCO (Systemic Sustainability Transition Solution for Health Care Organisations) is a European project funded under the Horizon Europe programme (Grant Agreement No. 101226802) and implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) scheme. The project aims to support health and care organisations in their transition towards more sustainable and environmentally responsible models by fostering the development of innovative digital solutions. Through the PCP process, suHCO will procure research and development services for the creation of an AI-enabled digital platform capable of helping healthcare organisations assess their sustainability performance, identify improvement opportunities, plan and implement actions, monitor progress, and support evidence-based decision-making. The future solution is expected to integrate sustainability knowledge, regulatory requirements, standards, best practices and relevant data sources, providing users with practical guidance tailored to their organisational context. It should also support sustainable procurement processes, impact assessment, reporting activities and organisational change management. The project is driven by a Buyers Group composed of healthcare organisations from Spain, Italy and Wales. The solutions developed during the PCP will be progressively designed, prototyped and validated in real healthcare environments to ensure their relevance, usability and scalability. By bringing together healthcare providers, technology developers and sustainability experts, suHCO seeks to stimulate innovation and contribute to the sustainability objectives of European health systems.

Water and milk is the recommended drink. The goal in the canteens, the largest buyer on the contract, is that the healthy alternatives and meals should be the most affordable and easily available. Increased use of goods produced in Inland and Norway shall also be facilitated. Sustainability, public health, democracy comprehension and life mastering are interdisciplinary topics that will permeate education in county schools. The framework agreements for food articles shall contribute to supporting the contracting authority ́s aims within these areas. The contracting authority would like to enter into agreements with tenderers who offer high quality, good service and relevant competence and who actively contribute to the desired consumption and ordering pattern. This includes good digital solutions, clear product information and labelling schemes, as well as offers of courses, guidance and statistics that can support informed choices at orderers and users. IFK would like tenderers to use the competition to show how their offer of product selection and prices, internet shop, brand schemes/information, campaigns, promotional measures, courses and/or consumption statistics can contribute to promoting the desired consumption and ordering pattern. At the same time, the procurement shall contribute to limiting the consumption of goods with low nutritional value, such as candy, snacks, sweet beverages and similar products. The Contracting Authority uses the Hyyr portal. This is where the competition is published, tender documentation will be published, communication will take place and additional information will be published. It is crucial that you have registered interest in the tender contest in Hyyr in order to participate in the communication and additional information that is published. description-proc.eng: The "Sustainable Energy Programme in Senegal" (PED III) is a technical cooperation project of the Senegalese Ministry of Energy, Oil and Mines (MEPM), financed by BMZ and implemented by GIZ. The project amounts to 7.500.000 EUR and runs from 01/2026 to 12/2028. The main implementing partners are, besides the MEPM, the Agence pour l'économie et la gestion de l'énergie (AEME), the Agence nationale des énergies renouvelables (ANER), the Agence sénégalaise de l'électrification rurale (ASER), the Commission de régulation du secteur de l'électricité (CRSE), the Compagnie nationale de l'électricité (SENELEC), the private sector and civil society. The aim of PED III is "to support the effective implementation of the Just Energy Transition by the main players in Senegal's public and private sectors at both strategic and operational levels". The project contributes to achieving the objectives of the national energy policy linked to renewable energy (RE) and energy efficiency (EE) for the implementation of the 2030 Agenda SDGs, in particular SDG 7 (access to energy), 8 (decent work and economic growth), 9 (industrialisation) and 13 (combating climate change), as well as German support for achieving the objectives of the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JET-P) signed between Senegal and the G7 in June 2023. The project's target groups are the public sector (ministries, national and decentralised authorities, training and research establishments) and the private sector (media, businesses, private sector support structures and women's socio-economic organisations). The Senegalese population will have greater access to a competitive and sustainable energy supply. New jobs linked to the fair energy transition are within the reach of women, young people and professionals, depending on their areas of expertise. At national level, the capacities of the Ministry of Energy and other stakeholders to steer the energy transition process will be strengthened. In addition, support for the operationalisation of the ecosystem enabling private investment in the transition will be supported. Lastly, the economic opportunities of the transition and the capacity-building required for its deployment will be promoted. The expected results of the project are as follows: 1. The coherent governance structure for RE & EE within JETP is strengthened. 2. The framework conditions for the integration of renewable energies into the grid and private investment in renewable energies and energy efficiency are improved 3. Public and private players have the necessary skills to implement inclusive energy transition projects.

The assignment shall support the aim of increased research efforts in business, several qualified applications for relevant research resources and better regional coverage in the mobilisation work. It is particularly important to mobilise research-independent companies in prioritised branches, facilitate more lasting co-operation relationships between businesses and R&D actors and contribute to the continuation of promising initiatives from early idea phases and preliminary projects to major development and research projects. Description of the assignment The contracting authority shall procure assistance from a total of five competence broker teams for research mobilisation in Troms. The resources shall collectively cover the topic areas seafood, space activity/space, KI and technology development as well as Circular Troms, where two of the sub-contracts shall be related to seafood. Each sub-contract shall be taken care of by a competence broker team with relevant and complementary competence within the relevant input area. The target group for the assignment is small and medium sized companies that belong to Troms county, or who have considerable activity in Troms. Competence brokering shall be a free offer to the target group. The assignment requires that the competence brokers act independently and neutrally and that they do not represent business actors who can be in a competitive relationship with the companies that receive assistance. The competence brokers shall sign a confidentiality statement. The delivery includes outreach contact with companies, needs analysis, mapping of relevant R&D partners, connection between companies and research environments as well as guidance in the development of R&D projects and applications for research resources. Follow-up shall be adapted to each company's need and maturity, and can include assistance from early idea clarification and preliminary project for further mobilisation with main projects and other relevant schemes. The competence broker shall be a consultant and supervisor in application processes, but shall not write applications on behalf of the companies or act in competition with private actors. The competence broker teams shall be able to identify the companies ́ need for research and innovation, contribute to finding relevant research competence and guide the companies towards appropriate sources of financing. This includes FORREGION and other relevant schemes, e.g. Tax Finds, The Research Council of Norway, Innovation Norway, Horizon Europe and other relevant means. Where it is natural, the competence brokers should also refer to other actors in the funding apparatus. The assignment includes further follow-up of companies that have previously carried out preliminary projects financed by FORREGION Troms, with the aim of contributing to further development and execution of main projects. The competence brokers shall also be able to arrange network meetings between businesses and R&D actors in order to identify common problems, possibilities for research and development, as well as strengthen the sharing of knowledge and cooperation. Resources are requested with relevant experience from research mobilisation in business, a good understanding of regional innovation and R&D environments, knowledge of relevant businesses in the region and the ability to work needs controlled. The role requires good collaboration abilities, good communication comprehension and the ability to build trust in both companies and research environments. The competence brokers shall furthermore cooperate with other competence brokers in FORREGION, other innovation actors in Troms and participate in relevant regional and national gatherings, including obligatory training and gathering activities managed by the Research Council of Norway. The assignment also includes reporting to the contracting authority through fixed digital reporting systems and templates. The reporting shall, among other things, provide an overview of completed mediations, resource use, contact with R&D institutions, projects that are brokered on to relevant schemes, preliminary projects, network meetings and other relevant results and activities.

title-proc.eng: Consultancy framework agreement for formulation, appraisal and review of Danish development cooperation programmes and projects

description-proc.eng: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA services at home in Copenhagen and abroad. In the procurement of individual contracts, they are responsible for the choice of procurement modality, the planning, preparation and management of the tender and contracting process. This process is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. AMGs contain the policies, guidelines, and tools for the MFA’s development cooperation assistance. They cover different forms of Danish development cooperation modalities. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The framework agreement is expected to solely cover bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects designed and implemented by Denmark. Therefore, the expected scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Aid (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is also expected to be divided into two lots. Under each lot, the MFA expects to conclude a framework agreement with between three to seven contractor to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during the term of the framework agreement, specifically the terms for award of contracts with/without reopening of competition amongst the contractors on the framework agreement. The expected lots reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate change, environment, private sector development, enabling environment and financing. Lot 2: Governance, response to conflicts, forced displacement, irregular migration, health and education. Each lot is expected to require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. The estimated values of the procurement and the lots are preliminary estimates.

title-proc.eng: 10040386-Mejorar mecanismos políticos, técnicos y financieros para escalar la gestión sostenible de suelos en Bolivia

description-proc.eng: In the Bolivian High Plateau ("Altiplano") rural families rely on agriculture, livestock farming, and other economic activities -such as tourism and trade- to sustain their livelihoods. However, an acute soil degradation, frosts, droughts, hailstorms, and strong winds reduce productivity and increase the vulnerability of rural communities. Compounding this issue is migration to urban centres and other regions from youth and women. According to the National Institute of Statistics (INE, 2025), more than 50% of rural families in the Altiplano live under poverty line, with limited access to technical, financial, and innovation services. All these factors result in greater vulnerability to climate change and a reduced adaptive capacity. In response Bolivia committed to achieve Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) by 2030 through soil restoration, climate resilience, and biodiversity conservation; under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Sustainable soil management is a fundamental pillar for restoring soil health and strengthening agrifood systems and ecosystems resilience. Hence, the German Cooperation together with national subnational stakeholders, producers and civil society organizations will implement the Sustainable Soil Management for agrifood system adaptation and resilience Project (SUAGRI) to foster soil management through a comprehensive approach. This approach includes strengthening the political, regulatory, and institutional framework; developing a soil information and monitoring system; fostering soil technological innovation; managing bioinputs; and ensuring access to public and private financing mechanisms to farmers. SUAGRI aims to improve and consolidate the political, regulatory, technical, and financial enable conditions to scale up sustainable soil management and biodiversity restoration in the Bolivian Altiplano. Thus, it contributes to increase agrifood systems and ecosystems resilience improving the livelihoods of households. SUAGRI proposes four components, described below: 1. Political and Regulatory Instruments: Improve norms and policy instruments to strengthen the regulatory framework, guiding territorial planning and public investments toward sustainable agricultural production. Through a participatory and multisectoral approach that brings together public, private, and local actors, it promotes policy coherence, inter-institutional coordination, and the integration of environmental, social, and economic criteria. 2. Soil Geoinformation: Generate and facilitate soil-related information to strengthen the availability, quality, and access to technical and scientific information for sustainable soil management. This enables better territorial and natural resource management. It also promotes the integration of traditional knowledge, with an emphasis on the participation of women and youth. 3. Financial mechanisms: Facilitate access to public and private financial mechanisms to scale up soil restoration and resilient agricultural production. This component is aimed at producers: micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), the private sector, and civil society organizations. . 4. Integrated Bioinputs Management: To increase the supply and demand for bio-inputs (such as compost, humus, among others), under sustainability criteria that contribute to soil recovery and health; biodiversity; and resilient agricultural production. This will be done with the participation of producer organizations and MSMEs, led primarily by women and rural youth.

title-proc.eng: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products

description-proc.eng: Iraq faces a persistent gap between its people and the financial system. Banks have long leaned on large state-owned institutions, credit has flowed mainly to established borrowers, and micro and small businesses along with women entrepreneurs and displaced communities have been largely left out. ProDIGI project, full name Promoting Employment in the Digital and Green Economy in Iraq, is trying to change that in a practical, grounded way. ProDIGI is a multi-donor initiative commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union, and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The project covers central and southern Iraq as well as the Kurdistan Region, with a focus on areas where joblessness, displacement, and limited access to services overlap. Within the project, Output 3 targets the financial inclusion side of the challenge. The starting point is a clear-eyed look at what the sector lacks: financial service providers that are capable, willing, and equipped to design products that fit the people they are supposed to serve. Banks and microfinance institutions in Iraq today mostly offer standardised products with high collateral requirements and limited digital capabilities. Reaching women led small businesses, rural communities, or young entrepreneurs running green or tech ventures requires a different kind of product, and often a different kind of institution. To bridge that gap, the project works directly with Iraqi financial service providers: banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment companies, fintechs, and government lending programmes. The approach combines needs assessments, hands-on advisory services, staff training, product design support, and pilot testing. The goal is not to deliver a finished product from outside, but to build the knowledge and process capacity within each institution so that change remains after the project ends. By the close of the assignment, at least three new or significantly adapted financial products must be in place, and these products must be actively reaching real users at a minimum of 950 individuals and 50 companies. The work also emphasises gender equality: women-led businesses are a priority target group, and all capacity-building activities must include a meaningful share of women participants. The broader context matters too. Iraq's Central Bank launched the national financial inclusion strategy that encourages digital payments, SME lending, and consumer protection improvements. ProDIGI project aligns directly with those priorities, making it both a practical intervention at the level of individual institutions and a contribution to the country's wider financial sector development. The selected firm will work directly with three to five financial service providers (FSPs) operating in Iraq. These may include commercial banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment providers, fintechs, and government lending schemes. GIZ will have pre-selected up to two FSPs before the contract starts, so work can begin without delay. The remaining FSPs will be selected by the contractor and GIZ jointly, based on agreed criteria.

It is, therefore, considered technically impossible or disproportionately difficult for other tenderers to join the contract without extensive re-programming, system integrations and the risk of interruption to operations. The costs associated with a supplier exchange will mean that only the current supplier will be able to deliver a competitive tender and that the costs and risk of operational disruptions associated with switching suppliers do not appear as a reasonable alternative. Sykehusinnkjøp HF carried out in mid-2026, on behalf of Helse Bergen HF, a market dialogue on the provision of services and materials connected to the service and operation of a uniform delivery and submission system for Helse Bergen HF. Link to a completed market dialogue: Uniform delivery and delivery system - service agreement - for Helse Bergen HF | Doffin, The Database for Public Procurements The systems at the health company was described and written feedback was requested from suppliers who could confirm their ability to provide services in accordance with the requirements specified in the market dialogue. No formal responses to the market dialogue were received by the deadline. However, the current supplier of the existing delivery and delivery system reported interest in the delivery. Based on the completed market dialogue and a lack of feedback from other actors, Sykehusinnkjøp HF and the health companies assess that there are no other known suppliers than Metalprogetti who are able to provide the services and products necessary for this delivery. Based on this, the terms for exemptions from competitions in accordance with the procurement regulations § 13-4 letters b points 2 and 3 are fulfilled, as, due to technical reasons, access to drawings and production of original spare parts, and due to possession of specific rights and tools, it is not possible to achieve real competition without inflicting disproportionate replacement costs and risks on the health authorities. The contract has an estimated value of NOK 1,500,000 excluding VAT for the entire contract period and a maximum value of NOK 1,900,000, excluding VAT. The contract will be valid from 01.12.2026 to 30.11.2028. Helse Bergen HF has a unilateral option to extend the contract for up to one (1) year at a time, up to eight (8) times. The maximum contract period is ten (10) years, including the option periods. Based on the equipment ́s need for service, maintenance, spare parts and technical support for the existing installations, the Contracting Authority has determined that the framework agreement period shall exceed four years. The facility constitutes critical infrastructure for the hospital's logistics functions, and considerations for continuity of operations, access to manufacturer-specific competence, software support and original spare parts indicate a longer contract period. It is therefore assessed that a maximum contract length of ten years is justifiable and necessary in order to ensure proper operation and management of the installation. Based on the result of the market dialogue, only Metalprogetti S.P.A is the relevant supplier for Helse Bergen HF. The contract will only apply to normal service and maintenance of existing installations and it will not include new installations for the companies ́locations. Helse Bergen HF therefore intends to enter into a contract with Metalprogetti S.P.A for the procurement of services and materials for uniform delivery and delivery system for Helse Bergen HF.
